title: SDK microcertification labs & practical exams — proposal
body:
Purpose
---
Quick proposal for a small, low-friction "microcertification" for internal engineers and newer partners who adopt Redwood SDKs. Goal: provide hands-on labs + short practical exams that verify core fluency (init, auth, streaming, error handling, telemetry hooks) without requiring a full course or heavy time investment. This is intended as an opt-in badge used by hiring/onboarding and solutions engineers to assess readiness for customer integrations.

Why this?
- We repeatedly see the same onboarding gaps in customer demos and pilots: missing retry logic, ignoring partial-stream handling, naive token budgeting.
- A quick, practical assessment is more predictive of success than a checklist doc.
- Microcerts are lightweight and can be iterated quickly; they can feed telemetry into the Console onboarding funnels.

Success metrics (first 6 months)
- 60% of new SEs and 15% of trial customers complete at least one lab within 30 days of signup.
- Average time-to-first-successful-integration reduced by 20% for participants.
- Reduction in common onboarding support tickets (auth, streaming, token budgeting) by 30% for accounts with microcertified engineers.

Scope (MVP)
- 3 labs (guided, runnable on local dev VM / GitHub Codespaces):
  1) QuickInit — init client, client-side config, first request + error handling (15–20 min)
  2) StreamSafe — streaming responses, partial-output handling, graceful cancellation (25–35 min)
  3) Cost-aware Patterns — batching/embeddings/quantization config example + telemetry hooks (30–40 min)
- 3 tiny practical exams (10–20 min each) that automatically evaluate via test harness (unit tests / smoke integration).
- Badging & short profile note in internal directory (not public yet).

Learning outcomes (per lab)
- QuickInit: create API key safely, wire client, perform a generation, detect and retry transient 429/502s, interpret latency metrics.
- StreamSafe: consume streaming tokens, assemble chunked JSON safely, avoid double-processing, implement timeout+cancel logic.
- Cost-aware Patterns: apply batching/prefix-caching heuristic, choose embedding model for retrieval latency vs cost, emit token-level telemetry tag.

Exam design notes
- Each exam is a short repo with a starter template and an autograder (GH actions + small local harness).
- Autograder checks: correct requests shape, correct retry/backoff semantics (mocked), correct handling of partial responses, basic telemetry events emitted (we check presence, not content privacy).
- Passing grade: 80% coverage of required checks. Optional higher-tier exam for "mentor" badge (90% + small architecture question).

Infra and runner options
- Local-first: encourage Codespaces or devcontainer so students run tests locally (no infra cost). Provide small fixture server that returns canned streaming events.
- Hosted quick-run: ephemeral Cloud runner (CI) that runs autograder on PRs for customers who want zero-local setup. Limit to 50 runs/day initially.
- Provide a Docker image with the SDK pinned to the current stable branch so environment drift is small.

Telemetry and reward model
- On passing, emit internal event to Console telemetry (user id, lab id, pass/fail) so we can correlate with adoption.
- Reward: internal badge + Slack emoji + entry in internal adopter tracker. Future: link to partner portal.

Rollout plan (Q1–Q2)
- Week 1–2: finalize lab repos (3) + autograder scaffolding. Internal alpha with 10 SEs.
- Week 3–4: collect feedback and iterate on failing cases; reduce flakiness in autograder.
- Week 5–8: open beta to new hires + 2 pilot customer teams (solutions-eng flagged).
- Month 3: evaluate telemetry, adjust passing criteria, prepare onboarding docs for SEs.

Operational concerns / anti-patterns
- Flaky autograders cause mistrust. Keep checks deterministic, avoid network calls in grader (use fixtures).
- Don’t try to teach advanced ML or prompt design — focus strictly on SDK integration mechanics.
- Privacy: never send real customer data to grader; use synthetic fixtures.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Badge surface area: internal-only vs shareable certificate? (Recommendation: internal-only for MVP.)
- Who owns upkeep of lab repos? (Propose eng-devexp + on-call rotation with 2-week cadence to address breakages.)
- Do we include a lightweight theory quiz? (Keep for v2; avoid blocking the practical exam.)

Minimal checklist (MVP)
- [ ] Repo skeletons for 3 labs (README + starter code + tests)
- [ ] Docker dev image built and published to our internal registry
- [ ] Example Codespace / devcontainer configured
- [ ] Autograder (GH action) + sample CI config
- [ ] Internal doc for SEs explaining purpose + how to enroll
- [ ] Telemetry event spec + Console dashboard stub (eng-observability ticket)
- [ ] Pilot group of 10 SEs + 2 customer pilot teams scheduled

Notes to self / rough invites
- Quick link deck for pilot: 10 slides, 5-min demo showing lab run + autograder pass. Target audience: solutions eng leads.
- Tagging: ping @marco in #devexp-onboard and drop a short survey for pilot feedback.
- Related tickets: ENG-1423 (Codespace infra), OBS-77 (telemetry event), DOC-56 (onboarding doc)

Grammar / UX rough ideas (short)
- Use task-oriented language in READMEs: "Do this, run this, expect that" with screenshots of console outputs for streaming lab.
- Provide an "I got stuck" small FAQ at the top of each lab pointing to common fixes.

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: low uptake. Mitigate by making the first lab <20 minutes and shipping it with new-hire onboarding flow.
- Risk: autograder complexity. Mitigate by starting with simple assertions and increasing sophistication later.

Next steps (this week)
1) Create repo skeleton + one lab draft (QuickInit) and open PR for internal review (owner: Aisha).
2) Marco to prototype Codespace config and a fixture streaming server (owner: Marco).
3) Jordan to draft telemetry event spec and Console dashboard stub (owner: Jordan).
4) Schedule 30-minute alpha demo with 10 SE volunteers (target week after next).

If this looks reasonable, I will spin up the QuickInit repo and drop links here. This doc is intentionally lightweight — prefer fast iteration over big upfront design.

Unresolved: automatic badge expiry and re-cert cadence — discuss at follow-up meeting.
